zones.label: CORPORATE IT NETWORK (Purdue L4–L5) · hybrid AD + Entra ID
OT NETWORK (Purdue L0–L3) · separate OT AD domain · water supply
Customer property (not on any utility network)

nodes.label: Entra ID
nodes.notes: Cloud identity for corporate staff — synced from the corporate AD. Has no knowledge of OT accounts.

nodes.label: OT access subnet
nodes.notes: The only corporate subnet allowed towards OT — and only by RDP to the IDMZ jump host. Dedicated hardened laptops; no email or web browsing.

nodes.label: Corp AD (hybrid)
nodes.notes: Corporate Active Directory forest — users, laptops, file shares. Synced to Entra ID. No trust with the OT domain.

nodes.label: SCADA integrator
nodes.notes: Supports SCADA and PLC logic under contract. Comes in over its own VPN to the IDMZ — never through the corporate network.

nodes.label: Billing provider
nodes.notes: Third-party customer billing. Gets customer reads from the AMI head-end and district bulk-flow figures from the IDMZ meter data gateway — never a route into OT.

nodes.label: AMI head-end
nodes.notes: Smart-meter network and head-end, run by the meter vendor/carrier. Entirely outside the OT network.

nodes.label: FW-1 · IT ↔ IDMZ
nodes.notes: North conduit. Permits only: OT access subnet → jump host (RDP); corporate users → historian replica (HTTPS); patch relay ← corporate WSUS/AV. Default deny.

nodes.label: Remote access GW
nodes.notes: Separate internet breakout for OT remote support. Accounts disabled by default, enabled per job, MFA, time-boxed.

nodes.label: Jump host
nodes.notes: Every interactive session into OT — staff or vendor — lands here first and is recorded. Uses OT AD accounts, not corporate ones.

nodes.label: Patch & AV relay
nodes.notes: Pulls approved patches and AV definitions from corporate IT through FW-1; OT pulls from here through FW-2 after vendor compatibility testing.

nodes.label: Meter data gateway
nodes.notes: Publishes district (DMA) bulk-flow figures, taken from the historian replica, for the billing provider to collect. The only thing billing can reach.

nodes.label: FW-2 · IDMZ ↔ OT
nodes.notes: South conduit. Permits only: jump host → engineering workstation; historian → replica (one-way); SCADA ← patch relay. Nothing from IT reaches OT without terminating in the IDMZ.

nodes.label: OT AD
nodes.notes: Separate OT Active Directory forest — not synced to Entra, no trust with corporate AD. A corporate compromise doesn't hand over OT logons.

nodes.label: Engineering WS
nodes.notes: PLC programming and SCADA configuration tools. Reached only through the jump host.

nodes.label: SCADA servers
nodes.notes: Supervises every site: polls PLCs at the works over the plant network and remote RTUs over telemetry. Alarms to the control room 24/7.

nodes.label: Works HMI
nodes.notes: Operators run the treatment works from here: filter backwash, dosing set-points, pump duty/standby.

nodes.label: Private APN
nodes.notes: Carrier private APN carrying telemetry between SCADA and remote outstations. Not internet-routable.

nodes.label: PLC · dosing
nodes.notes: Closed loop: trims chlorine dose to hold the set-point residual measured by the analysers; alarms and trips dosing on high/low residual.

nodes.label: Reservoir RTU
nodes.notes: Reports service-reservoir level and runs the booster pumps; reaches SCADA over the private APN.

nodes.label: Clarify & filter
nodes.notes: Coagulant dosing, flocculation, clarification and rapid-gravity sand filters.

nodes.label: Chlorine dosing
nodes.notes: Sodium hypochlorite for disinfection, plus pH correction. Contact tank gives the required disinfection time.

nodes.label: DMA meter
nodes.notes: District meter area inlet: bulk flow meter (leakage and billing reconciliation) and pressure-reducing valve.

nodes.label: Customer home
nodes.notes: What the customer controls: the internal stopcock (shut off their supply) and their taps. They can see usage in the billing provider's app — nothing upstream of the meter.

steps.note: A regional water company split along the Purdue model: the corporate IT network on top (L4–L5), the OT control network below (L0–L3), and an industrial DMZ (L3.5) between them. Third parties sit outside both.
Corporate IT (L4–L5): internet, Microsoft 365, office users, ERP and the corporate AD. Nothing here talks to a PLC.

Two separate Active Directories. Corporate AD is hybrid — Entra Connect syncs it to Entra ID for M365. OT has its own AD forest: not synced to the cloud, no trust with corporate, separate admin accounts.
The IDMZ (L3.5) sits between two firewalls, ideally from different vendors. Every flow between IT and OT terminates on a server here — nothing passes straight through.

The one corporate subnet that can reach OT: VLAN 50, a handful of hardened OT engineer laptops. It may only RDP to the jump host; from there, with an OT AD account, through FW-2 to the engineering workstation.

Vendor remote support: the SCADA integrator connects over its own VPN to a separate remote access gateway in the IDMZ — not via the corporate network — then through the same recorded jump host. Accounts stay off until a job is approved.

Third-party billing never touches OT. Customer reads go from the smart meter to the vendor-hosted AMI head-end and on to billing; district bulk-flow figures are pulled from a meter data gateway in the IDMZ.
Business reporting works the same way: the OT historian pushes one-way through FW-2 to a replica in the IDMZ, and corporate users read the replica through FW-1 — never the live historian.
L3, site operations: SCADA servers, the OT historian, the engineering workstation and the OT AD. Patches arrive only from the IDMZ relay after testing.
L2 and L1: the works HMI drives PLCs over the plant network. Remote sites use RTUs — the intake over licensed radio, the service reservoir over a private 4G APN back to SCADA.
L0, the water itself: raw water is pumped from the upland reservoir into the treatment works, then clarified and filtered.
Chemical treatment: chlorine (sodium hypochlorite) and pH correction are dosed, and analysers measure the residual. PLC-20 closes the loop — a tampered set-point here is a public-health event.

Treated water is pumped to the service reservoir, boosted into the network, metered at the DMA and piped to the customer — who sits outside every utility network and controls only their stopcock and taps.
